question: Should an attacker be offside only when there is clear daylight between him and the defender?
answer: Offside exists to stop goal-hanging, not to cancel goals over a toenail. Camera frames, and a kick point that can be misjudged by one frame, cannot honestly separate bodies a few centimetres apart. A daylight rule would restore the benefit of the doubt, keep celebrations spontaneous and make attackers gamble on early runs again.
move: Whichever side you took, whether any margin just creates a new borderline decides it.
ask: If I add a margin to a hard line, have I just made a new borderline case?
counterpoint: Daylight only moves the line: there will still be a sliver between some daylight and none, and defenders would lose the offside trap, since holding a line would no longer catch a runner half a body ahead. With video review, one study found key refereeing decisions rose from about 92% to about 98% correct.
source: Spitz et al., Journal of Sports Sciences, 2021
reference: Spitz, Wagemans, Memmert, Williams & Helsen, Video assistant referees (VAR): the impact of technology on decision making in association football referees, Journal of Sports Sciences, 2021
